title.zh: 卷375 列傳一百六十二 白镕 孙桓 史致俨 那清安 升寅 李宗昉 姚元之 何汝霖 季芝昌 列傳
title.en: Volume 375 Biographies 162: Bai Rong, Sun Huan, Shi Zhiyan, Na Qingan, Sheng Yin, Li Zongfang, Yao Yuanzhi, He Rulin, Ji Zhichang, Lie Chuan
title.raw: 卷375 列傳一百六十二 白镕 孙桓 史致俨 那清安 升寅 李宗昉 姚元之 何汝霖 季芝昌 列傳

sentences.zh: 白鎔，字小山，順天通州人。

translations.literal: Bai Rong, style name Xiaoshan, was a native of Tongzhou in Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: Bai Rong, whose courtesy name was Xiaoshan, came from Tongzhou in the Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，典福建鄉試。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed compiler, and presided over the Fujian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi degree in the fourth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy as a bachelor, was made a compiler, and served as chief examiner for the Fujian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 十八年，大考二等，擢贊善。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, in the grand examination he placed in the second class and was promoted to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In his eighteenth year of service he ranked second class in the palace examination and was promoted to tutor in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 督安徽學政，詔密詢地方利弊，疏言：「安徽錢糧，惟鳳陽、泗州遭湖、河之害，積逋較巨。

translations.literal: As superintendent of Anhui education he was secretly ordered to inquire into local advantages and disadvantages, and memorialized: "In Anhui grain taxes, only Fengyang and Sizhou suffered harm from lakes and rivers, and their accumulated arrears were comparatively large.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as Anhui educational commissioner he was secretly instructed to report on local conditions; he memorialized: "Among Anhui's land-tax obligations, only Fengyang and Sizhou, battered by floods from lakes and rivers, carried unusually heavy arrears.

sentences.zh: 遇豐稔之年，循例帶徵舊額。

translations.literal: In years of abundant harvest, by precedent they would levy collection of the old quotas as well.
translations.idiomatic: In bumper years officials still followed precedent and collected outstanding quotas along with the current levy.

sentences.zh: 在小民以一年而輸數年之賦，雖樂歲不免拮据；

translations.literal: For the common people to pay several years' taxes in one year, even in a good year they could not avoid strain;
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary households were thus asked to pay several years' taxes in a single season, so that even a prosperous year left them strapped;

sentences.zh: 而官吏懼譴，規避多方，積重難返。

translations.literal: while officials, fearing punishment, employed many evasions, and the accumulated burden became hard to reverse.
translations.idiomatic: while magistrates, dreading censure, devised endless dodges until the burden grew too entrenched to lift.

sentences.zh: 與其存徵之名，緻小民日受追呼，國計依然無補，何如核徵之實，使官吏從容措理，舊額尚可漸清。

translations.literal: Rather than keeping the name of collection and causing the common people daily to suffer pursuit and summons while state revenue still gained nothing, why not verify actual collection, let officials handle matters at ease, and the old quotas could still be gradually cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Better to collect what was truly due than to preserve the fiction of arrears while commoners faced daily dunning with no gain to the treasury; if collectors worked from verified figures, old quotas might still be cleared over time.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後二屬錢糧，每年祗帶徵一年，儻遇歉收，再行遞緩，民力漸紓，催科者自顧考成，行之必有效。

translations.literal: He requested that hereafter for the two prefectures' grain taxes, each year only one year's arrears be collected in addition; if harvest failed, further deferral; popular strength would gradually ease; those pressing collection would themselves mind their performance evaluation—implementing this would certainly be effective.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that thereafter these two prefectures collect at most one year of arrears per annum, deferring further if the harvest failed, so that popular strength could recover and tax agents, mindful of their own evaluations, would enforce the rule—this, he said, would surely work.

sentences.zh: 」詔允行。

translations.literal: " An edict approved implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved and ordered it carried out.

sentences.zh: 青陽有孝子曰徐守仁，幼孤，事母孝。

translations.literal: In Qingyang there was a filial son named Xu Shouren, orphaned young, who served his mother filially.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingyang lived a filial son named Xu Shouren, who lost his father early yet served his mother with exemplary devotion.

sentences.zh: 母沒，廬墓三年，鎔造廬贈賻，題請旌表。

translations.literal: When his mother died, he dwelt at the tomb for three years; Rong built a mourning hut and gave funeral gifts, and submitted a request for imperial commendation.
translations.idiomatic: After her death he mourned at the grave for three years; Rong built a hut for him, gave funeral gifts, and petitioned for an imperial commendation.

sentences.zh: 訪求明臣左光斗遺裔，取列縣庠。

translations.literal: He sought out descendants of the Ming minister Zuo Guangdou and enrolled them in the district school.
translations.idiomatic: He searched out descendants of the Ming minister Zuo Guangdou and enrolled them in the district academy.

sentences.zh: 按試所至，集士人講學，以正人心厚風俗為本。

translations.literal: Wherever he examined scholars, he gathered literati to lecture, taking rectification of hearts and thickening customs as the foundation.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he conducted examinations he gathered scholars for lectures, aiming above all to rectify hearts and strengthen local morals.

sentences.zh: 累遷少詹事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to junior mentor of the heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to junior mentor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，督廣東學政。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he served as superintendent of Guangdong education.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed educational commissioner for Guangdong.

sentences.zh: 歷詹事、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served as mentor and grand secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of mentor of the heir apparent and bachelor of the Grand Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 七年，擢工部侍郎，調吏部。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was promoted vice minister of works and transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made vice minister of works, then transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，偕尚書松筠赴直隸按外委白勤被誣冤斃獄，護理總督屠之申以下降黜有差。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, together with Minister Songyun he went to Zhili to investigate the case of sub-official Bai Qin, who had been wrongfully killed in prison on false charges; Acting Governor Tu Zhichao and those below were demoted to varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he joined Minister Songyun in Zhili to review the case of sub-official Bai Qin, executed in prison on a false charge; Acting Governor Tu Zhichao and subordinates were demoted in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 督江蘇學政。

translations.literal: He served as superintendent of Jiangsu education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Jiangsu educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 尋偕侍郎寶興勘視南河垛料，舉實以聞。

translations.literal: Soon after, together with Vice Minister Bao Xing he inspected the stacked materials of the Southern Canal and reported the facts.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Vice Minister Bao Xing in inspecting stockpiles along the Southern Canal and reported what they found.

sentences.zh: 十一年，擢左都御史，召還京，未至，命查勘江南災賑。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was promoted Left Censor-in-Chief and summoned back to the capital; before he arrived he was ordered to investigate Jiangnan disaster relief.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was promoted to Left Censor-in-Chief and recalled to the capital, but before he arrived was sent to inspect disaster relief in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 時尚書穆彰阿、硃士彥亦奉命勘湖、河汎溢狀，穆彰阿先回京，鎔遂偕士彥履勘沿河閘壩工程，與總督陶澍定議以工代賑。

translations.literal: At the time Ministers Mujangga and Zhu Shiyan were also ordered to survey lake and river overflow; Mujangga returned to the capital first, and Rong then with Zhu Shiyan toured and inspected sluice-gate and dam works along the river, and with Governor Tao Shu decided on relief through labor.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers Mujangga and Zhu Shiyan were then surveying flood damage on lakes and rivers; Mujangga returned first, and Rong with Zhu Shiyan inspected river sluices and dams, agreeing with Governor Tao Shu to substitute public works for relief grain.

sentences.zh: 赴安徽，週曆太平、寧國、池州、安慶、廬州各郡，先後疏劾飾災侵賑諸弊。

translations.literal: He went to Anhui, toured Taiping, Ningguo, Chizhou, Anqing, Luzhou and other prefectures, and successively memorialized impeachments for the abuses of feigning disaster and embezzling relief.
translations.idiomatic: In Anhui he toured Taiping, Ningguo, Chizhou, Anqing, Luzhou, and other prefectures, memorializing in turn officials who padded disaster reports or stole relief funds.

sentences.zh: 次年，回京，署翰林院掌院學士，典順天鄉試。

translations.literal: The following year he returned to the capital, acted as chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and presided over the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he returned to the capital, served as acting chancellor of the Hanlin Academy, and presided over the Shuntian provincial examination.

sentences.zh: 十三年，擢工部尚書，典武會試。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was promoted Minister of Works and presided over the military metropolitan examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became Minister of Works and chief examiner for the military metropolitan examination.

sentences.zh: 故事，武闈雙好不足額，始取單好。

translations.literal: By precedent, if double-excellence candidates in the military examination did not fill the quota, only then were single-excellence candidates taken.
translations.idiomatic: By custom, when candidates excelling in both archery and horsemanship did not fill the military quota, single-excellence candidates were admitted.

sentences.zh: 是科雙好不盡取中，坐降大理寺卿。

translations.literal: That session did not fully select all double-excellence candidates; he was penalized by demotion to chief of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: That year not all double-excellence candidates were passed; he was demoted to chief of the Court of Judicial Review for the lapse.

sentences.zh: 十九年，乞病歸，卒於家，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he begged leave on grounds of illness and returned home; he died at home, age seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he retired on grounds of illness and died at home at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 鎔事母孝，教子弟嚴。

translations.literal: Rong was filial toward his mother and strict in instructing his sons and nephews.
translations.idiomatic: Rong was devoted to his mother and stern in raising his sons and nephews.

sentences.zh: 宣宗嘗嘉其家法之善，以勉朝臣雲。

translations.literal: The Xuanzong Emperor once praised the goodness of his household regulations to encourage court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuanzong once praised his household discipline as a model for the court.

sentences.zh: 孫桓，字建侯。

translations.literal: Sun Huan, style name Jianhou.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Huan, courtesy name Jianhou.

sentences.zh: 同治二年進士，授吏部主事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tongzhi he passed the jinshi examination and was appointed a principal in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi degree in the second year of Tongzhi and was appointed a principal clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to director.

sentences.zh: 掌選，清嚴慎密，吏不能欺，為時所稱。

translations.literal: In charge of selections, he was clear, strict, and meticulous; clerks could not deceive him, and he was praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Overseeing appointments, he was lucid, strict, and meticulous; clerks could not fool him, and contemporaries praised his integrity.

sentences.zh: 光緒中，洊擢兵部侍郎，綜覈一如為司官時。

translations.literal: In the Guangxu reign he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of war, and his overall review was as when he had been a bureau officer.
translations.idiomatic: Under Guangxu he was repeatedly promoted to vice minister of war, reviewing cases with the same rigor he had shown as a bureau officer.

sentences.zh: 十七年，因病乞休，尋卒。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he begged leave on grounds of illness; soon after he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he asked to retire for illness and soon died.

sentences.zh: 史致儼，字容莊，江蘇江都人。

translations.literal: Shi Zhiyan, style name Rongzhuang, was a native of Jiangdu in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Zhiyan, whose courtesy name was Rongzhuang, came from Jiangdu in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 家酷貧。

translations.literal: His family was extremely poor.
translations.idiomatic: His family was desperately poor.

sentences.zh: 甫冠，為諸生，學政謝墉器其才，給膏火，居尊經閣讀書。

translations.literal: Just after coming of age he became a licentiate; Educational Commissioner Xie Yong valued his talent, supplied stipend, and had him read in the Zunjing Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after his capping ceremony he became a licentiate; Commissioner Xie Yong admired his talent, gave him a stipend, and lodged him in the Zunjing Pavilion to study.

sentences.zh: 薦預召試，未與選。

translations.literal: Recommended for the special summons examination, he was not selected.
translations.idiomatic: He was recommended for the special palace examination but was not chosen.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶四年，成進士，選庶吉士，授編修。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, and was appointed compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He received his jinshi in the fourth year of Jiaqing, entered the Hanlin Academy, and was made a compiler.

sentences.zh: 督四川學政。

translations.literal: He served as superintendent of Sichuan education.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Sichuan educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 累遷右庶子。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to right vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，督河南學政。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he served as superintendent of Henan education.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made Henan educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 自滑縣匪平，猶有伏莽，密詔偵察。

translations.literal: Since the bandits in Huaxian had been pacified, hidden malcontents still remained, and he was secretly ordered to investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Although the Huaxian rebels had been suppressed, covert troublemakers remained, and he received secret orders to investigate.

sentences.zh: 疏陳彰、衛二郡民間習邪教猶眾，州縣編查保甲，有名無實，撰敦俗篇，刊布以化導之。

translations.literal: He memorialized that in Zhang and Wei prefectures the people still widely practiced heterodox cults; prefectures and counties compiled baojia registers in name only; he composed a piece on renewing customs and published it to guide and transform them.
translations.idiomatic: He reported that heterodox sects still flourished in Zhang and Wei; local baojia registers were empty formalities; he wrote an essay on renewing customs and circulated it for moral instruction.

sentences.zh: 商丘廩生陳忠錦以不濫保被毆，知府、經歷受賕，反加斥責，忿而自經。

translations.literal: Chen Zhongjin, a grain-student of Shangqiu, was beaten for refusing to give indiscriminate guarantees; the prefect and the intendant's clerk took bribes and instead rebuked him; in anger he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhongjin, a Shangqiu grain-student, was beaten for refusing false guarantees; the prefect and intendant's clerk took bribes and blamed him instead; he hanged himself in outrage.

sentences.zh: 疏劾，譴罪有差。

translations.literal: He memorialized impeachment; punishments were meted out in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached the officials involved, and they were punished in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，典湖北鄉試。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he presided over the Hubei provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Daoguang he served as chief examiner for Hubei.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢刑部侍郎，調禮部。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted vice minister of punishments and transferred to the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he became vice minister of punishments, then moved to the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，督福建學政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he served as superintendent of Fujian education.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was appointed Fujian educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 奏分台灣舉人中額，增所屬四縣學額。

translations.literal: He memorialized to divide the Taiwan quota for juren and increase school quotas in its four subordinate counties.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed allotting juren quotas separately for Taiwan and increasing academy seats in its four counties.

sentences.zh: 漳、泉諸郡習械鬥，諸生與者，屏不與試，悍風稍息。

translations.literal: Zhang and Quan prefectures were accustomed to armed brawls; students who took part were barred from examinations, and the violent custom gradually subsided.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang and Quan were notorious for armed feuds; students involved were barred from examinations, and the violence gradually eased.

sentences.zh: 九年，偕侍郎鍾昌赴山西鞫獄，平定知州故出人罪，鞫實，論兇犯如律，褫知州恆傑職。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, together with Vice Minister Zhong Chang he went to Shanxi to try a case; the Pingding prefect had improperly released persons from guilt; the facts were established, the chief culprits were sentenced according to law, and Prefect Heng Jie was stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he and Vice Minister Zhong Chang tried a case in Shanxi where the Pingding prefect had unlawfully freed criminals; the facts were proved, ringleaders were sentenced by law, and Prefect Heng Jie was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 調刑部，歷左都御史，遷禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments, served as Left Censor-in-Chief, and was promoted Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to the Ministry of Punishments, became Left Censor-in-Chief, then Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 兩典順天鄉試。

translations.literal: He twice presided over the Shuntian provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He twice served as chief examiner for Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 調工部，又調刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Works, then again to Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was shifted to Works, then back to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 勤於其職，竟日坐堂上閱案牘，揅析論難，視司員如弟子。

translations.literal: Diligent in duty, he sat in court all day reviewing case documents, analyzing and debating difficult points, and treated bureau officers like disciples.
translations.idiomatic: Conscientious in office, he spent whole days in court reviewing dossiers, debating fine points of law, and treating junior officers like pupils.

sentences.zh: 任刑部凡四年，京察，以刑名詳慎，被議敘。

translations.literal: He served in the Ministry of Punishments for four years; at the capital evaluation he was commended for meticulous care in criminal matters.
translations.idiomatic: After four years in Punishments, the capital evaluation commended his careful handling of criminal cases.

sentences.zh: 十八年，乞解職。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he requested to resign.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，年七十九，贈太子太保，祀鄉賢及名宦祠。

translations.literal: Soon after he died, age seventy-nine; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and enshrined in the local worthies' and eminent officials' temples.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at seventy-nine, was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and entered the local worthies' and eminent officials' shrines.

sentences.zh: 那清安，字竹汀，葉赫納喇氏，滿洲正白旗人。

translations.literal: Na Qing'an, style name Zhuting, of the Yehe Nara clan, was a Bannerman of the Plain White.
translations.idiomatic: Na Qing'an, courtesy name Zhuting, of the Yehe Nara clan, was a Plain White Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士，授戶部主事，遷翰林院侍講。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was appointed a principal in the Ministry of Revenue, and was promoted Hanlin academy expositor.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in the tenth year of Jiaqing, entered the Ministry of Revenue as a principal, and became a Hanlin expositor.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，授禮部侍郎，歷刑部、工部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he was appointed vice minister of rites and served in the ministries of punishments and works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he became vice minister of rites and later held posts in Punishments and Works.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，命赴直隸讞獄，擢左都御史，管光祿寺事，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was ordered to Zhili to try cases, was promoted Left Censor-in-Chief, managed the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and concurrently served as banner commander.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang's first year he was sent to try cases in Zhili, made Left Censor-in-Chief, oversaw the Court of Imperial Entertainments, and served concurrently as banner commander.

sentences.zh: 尋遷兵部尚書，調刑部。

translations.literal: Soon after he was promoted Minister of War and transferred to the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Minister of War, then transferred to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為熱河都統，偕左都御史松筠等赴土默特讞獄，事竣，疏言：「蒙古惡習，常有移屍訛詐，為害滋甚。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he went out as commander at Rehe; together with Left Censor-in-Chief Songyun and others he went to Tumed to try cases; when finished he memorialized: "Among Mongol bad customs, shifting corpses to extort is common and the harm is severe.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he became Rehe commander; with Left Censor-in-Chief Songyun he tried cases among the Tumed Mongols and then memorialized: "A vicious Mongol practice is to move corpses to frame others and extort money.

sentences.zh: 蒙古律例，凡軍流徒犯，罪止折枷，情重法輕。

translations.literal: Under Mongol statutes, for military exile, banishment, and penal servitude the punishment stops at commuted cangue; where the circumstances are grave the law is light.
translations.idiomatic: Under Mongol law, military exile, banishment, and penal servitude are routinely commuted to cangue, so serious cases receive light penalties.

sentences.zh: 請嗣後遇有假捏人命詐財者，所擬軍流徒罪即行實發，不准折枷，以懲刁惡。

translations.literal: He requested that hereafter when persons fabricate deaths to extort property, the proposed sentences of military exile, banishment, or penal servitude be actually carried out, with no commuted cangue, to punish craftiness and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: He asked that hereafter anyone who staged a death to extort money serve the full sentence of exile or penal servitude without commutation, to curb such fraud.

sentences.zh: 」下所司議行。

translations.literal: " The matter was referred to the responsible offices for deliberation and implementation.
translations.idiomatic: " The memorial was sent to the relevant offices for enactment.

sentences.zh: 六年，召授左都御史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was recalled and made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 逾年，復任熱河都統，召對，詢知其母年老，命仍還左都御史任。

translations.literal: After more than a year he again took office as commander at Rehe; summoned to audience, the emperor learned his mother was elderly and ordered him to return to the post of Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he resumed command at Rehe; at audience the emperor learned his mother was aged and sent him back to the Left Censor-in-Chief post instead.

sentences.zh: 十一年，复授兵部尚書，典順天鄉試及會試。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was again appointed Minister of War and presided over the Shuntian provincial and metropolitan examinations.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he again became Minister of War and chief examiner for Shuntian and the metropolitan examinations.

sentences.zh: 十四年，以疾乞解職，允之。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he begged to resign on grounds of illness; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he retired for illness, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈太子太保，諡恭勤。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Gongqin.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and received the posthumous name Gongqin.

sentences.zh: 那清安工為館體應制詩，時皆誦習。

translations.literal: Na Qing'an was skilled at composing regulated court poetry in the academy style, and his works were widely recited.
translations.idiomatic: Na Qing'an excelled at regulated court poetry in the academy manner, and his compositions were widely memorized.

sentences.zh: 因與穆彰阿同榜成進士，晚乃受宣宗知，迭秉文衡。

translations.literal: Because he had passed the jinshi in the same session as Mujangga, he only late in life won the Xuanzong Emperor's notice and repeatedly held literary examinations.
translations.idiomatic: A jinshi of the same year as Mujangga, he won Emperor Xuanzong's favor only late in life and repeatedly oversaw civil examinations.

sentences.zh: 既卒，會兵部以慶廉送武會試有殘疾，為監試御史所劾。

translations.literal: After his death, the Ministry of War was impeached for presenting Qinglian to the military metropolitan examination with a physical disability.
translations.idiomatic: After his death the Ministry of War was impeached for entering Qinglian in the military metropolitan examination despite a physical disability.

sentences.zh: 先是那清安為監射大臣，曾以慶廉殘疾扣除，上追念其持正，予其子全慶加二級。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Na Qing'an had been supervising archery as grand minister, he had disqualified Qinglian for disability; the emperor, recalling his uprightness, granted his son Quanqing an additional two ranks.
translations.idiomatic: When Na Qing'an had supervised the archery examination he had struck Qinglian from the rolls for disability; the emperor, remembering his firmness, granted his son Quanqing two additional ranks.

sentences.zh: 全慶，光緒初官大學士，自有傳。

translations.literal: Quanqing, in the early Guangxu reign, became a grand secretary and has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Quanqing became a grand secretary in early Guangxu and has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 昇寅，字賓旭，馬佳氏，滿洲鑲黃旗人。

translations.literal: Sheng Yin, style name Binxu, of the Maja clan, was a Bannerman of the Bordered Yellow.
translations.idiomatic: Sheng Yin, courtesy name Binxu, of the Maja clan, was a Bordered Yellow Banner Manchu.

sentences.zh: 拔貢，考授禮部七品小京官。

translations.literal: Selected as a tribute student, he passed examination and was appointed a seventh-rank secretary in the Ministry of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Having graduated as a tribute student, he passed the selection examination and became a seventh-rank secretary in the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 舉嘉慶五年鄉試。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the fifth year of Jiaqing.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial examination in the fifth year of Jiaqing.

sentences.zh: 累遷員外郎，改御史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to vice director and was transferred to censor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice director, then became a censor.

sentences.zh: 疏言學校為人才根本，請嚴課程，務實用，戒奢靡；

translations.literal: He memorialized that schools are the root of talent and requested strict curricula, practical learning, and restraint of luxury;
translations.idiomatic: He argued that schools are the foundation of talent and urged stricter curricula, practical study, and restraint of extravagance;

sentences.zh: 又疏陳防禁考試八旗生懷挾冒替諸弊：從之。

translations.literal: he also memorialized on preventing abuses in examinations among Banner students, such as carrying crib notes and impersonation: approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: he also proposed measures against cheating by Banner students in examinations, including hidden notes and impersonation, and the throne approved.

sentences.zh: 改右庶子，累遷副都御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right vice director of the Secretariat and was repeatedly promoted to vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He became right vice director of the Secretariat and rose to vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授盛京禮部侍郎，署盛京將軍。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed vice minister of rites at Mukden and acted as commander at Mukden.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made Mukden vice minister of rites and acting Mukden commander.

sentences.zh: 調刑部，召為工部侍郎，又調刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to the Ministry of Punishments, summoned as vice minister of works, then again transferred to punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Punishments, was recalled as vice minister of works, then returned to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 道光六年，出為熱河都統。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Daoguang he went out as commander at Rehe.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Daoguang he was posted as Rehe commander.

sentences.zh: 以蒙古各旗招內地遊民開採煤礦，往往生事械鬥，疏請諭禁，從之。

translations.literal: Because Mongol banners recruited inland migrants to open coal mines, which often led to armed brawls, he memorialized requesting prohibition, and approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol banners were hiring inland migrants to mine coal, often sparking armed fights; he memorialized for a ban, which was approved.

sentences.zh: 八年，命赴甘肅偕總督鄂山按寧夏將軍慶山、副都統噶普唐阿互劾事，罷慶山，即以昇寅代之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was ordered to Gansu with Governor Eshan to investigate the mutual impeachment of Ningxia Commander Qing Shan and Vice Commander Gaputang'a; Qing Shan was dismissed and Sheng Yin replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he joined Governor Eshan in Gansu to settle the mutual charges between Ningxia Commander Qing Shan and Vice Commander Gaputang'a; Qing Shan was removed and Sheng Yin took his place.

sentences.zh: 歷成都、綏遠城將軍。

translations.literal: He served as commander at Chengdu and Suiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded at Chengdu and Suiyuan.

sentences.zh: 命鞫鄂爾多斯京控獄，奏言：「蒙古京控日繁，請自後各部落封禁地樹立界牌，以杜私墾；

translations.literal: Ordered to try an appeal case from Ordos at the capital, he memorialized: "Capital appeals from Mongolia grow daily; hereafter let boundary markers be set on sealed lands of each tribe to stop illegal cultivation;
translations.idiomatic: Trying an Ordos appeal at the capital, he reported: "Mongol appeals to Beijing grow daily; boundary markers should be set on each tribe's sealed pasture to stop illegal farming;

sentences.zh: 蒙古阿勒巴圖禁止餽贈，以息爭端；

translations.literal: for Mongol commoners, gifts should be forbidden to end disputes;
translations.idiomatic: Mongol commoners should be barred from giving gifts that breed lawsuits;

sentences.zh: 扎薩克王、貝勒等毋用內地書吏，以免教唆；

translations.literal: princes, beile, and the like should not employ inland clerks, lest they be taught to sue;
translations.idiomatic: princes and beile should not hire inland clerks who teach them to litigate;

sentences.zh: 各旗協理台吉，會同盟長選舉，以昭慎重；

translations.literal: for assistant princes in each banner, election should be by league chiefs in joint council to show deliberation;
translations.idiomatic: assistant banner princes should be chosen jointly by league chiefs and elders to ensure care.

sentences.zh: 盟長會盟需用烏拉，應明定限制，以免浮索：庶積弊清而獄訟息。

translations.literal: When league chiefs met in alliance they required ula [ceremonial gifts]; limits should be clearly set to avoid excessive demands, so that accumulated abuses might be cleared and lawsuits cease.
translations.idiomatic: League chiefs' alliance meetings required ceremonial gifts; he urged fixed limits on such demands so old abuses and lawsuits might end.

sentences.zh: 十一年，召授左都御史，兼都統。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he was summoned and appointed Left Censor-in-Chief, concurrently serving as banner commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was recalled as Left Censor-in-Chief and concurrent banner commander.

sentences.zh: 十二年，署工部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he acted as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he served as acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 京畿旱，疏請發米，設十廠煮粥以濟災民，從之。

translations.literal: The capital region suffered drought; he memorialized to issue grain and set up ten kitchens for congee to relieve disaster victims; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: When drought struck the capital region he asked to release grain and open ten congee kitchens for the afflicted, and the request was approved.

sentences.zh: 十三年，偕侍郎鄂順安按西安將軍徐錕貪縱，得實，議褫職。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, together with Vice Minister Eshun'an he investigated Xi'an Commander Xu Kun for corruption and indulgence; the facts were established and dismissal was proposed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he and Vice Minister Eshun'an investigated Xi'an Commander Xu Kun for corruption and lax discipline, proved the charges, and recommended his removal.

sentences.zh: 十四年，命閱兵山東、河南，就鞫桐柏知縣寧飛濱故出人罪，治如律。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was ordered to review troops in Shandong and Henan, and on the way tried the case of Tongbai Prefect Ning Feibin, who had improperly released persons from guilt; he was sentenced according to law.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he inspected troops in Shandong and Henan and tried Tongbai Prefect Ning Feibin for unlawfully freeing criminals, sentencing him by law.

sentences.zh: 命赴廣東、湖南按事，授禮部尚書，未至，卒於途。

translations.literal: He was ordered to Guangdong and Hunan to investigate affairs, was appointed Minister of Rites, but before arriving died on the road.
translations.idiomatic: Sent to investigate affairs in Guangdong and Hunan, he was appointed Minister of Rites but died en route before taking office.

sentences.zh: 優詔賜卹，稱其老成清介，贈太子太保，諡勤直。

translations.literal: A gracious edict granted condolence payments, praising his mature integrity; he was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and the posthumous title Qinzhi.
translations.idiomatic: The throne granted special mourning favors, praising his seasoned integrity, posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, and gave him the posthumous name Qinzhi.

sentences.zh: 子寶琳，直隸保定知府，濬定州洿澤，有治績；

translations.literal: His son Baolin was prefect of Baoding in Zhili, dredged the foul marshes of Dingzhou, and had achievements in governance;
translations.idiomatic: His son Baolin, prefect of Baoding in Zhili, dredged Dingzhou's stagnant marshes with notable success;

sentences.zh: 寶珣，同治中，官兵部侍郎、山海關副都統。

translations.literal: Baoxun, in the Tongzhi reign, served as vice minister of war and vice commander at Shanhaiguan.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxun under Tongzhi was vice minister of war and vice commander at Shanhaiguan.

sentences.zh: 孫紹祺，咸豐六年進士，由編修官至理籓院尚書；

translations.literal: His grandson Shaoqi, jinshi in the sixth year of Xianfeng, rose from compiler to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Shaoqi, a Xianfeng sixth-year jinshi, rose from compiler to minister of the Court of Colonial Affairs;

sentences.zh: 紹諴，光緒中，山西布政使，從治鄭州河工，終駐藏大臣；

translations.literal: Shaoxuan, in the Guangxu reign, was Shanxi financial commissioner, took part in the Zhengzhou river works, and ended as resident commissioner in Tibet;
translations.idiomatic: Shaoxuan under Guangxu was Shanxi financial commissioner, helped on the Zhengzhou river project, and finished as Tibet resident commissioner;

sentences.zh: 紹英，宣統初，度支部侍郎，內務府大臣。

translations.literal: Shaoying, in early Xuantong, was vice minister of the Revenue Board and minister of the Imperial Household.
translations.idiomatic: Shaoying in early Xuantong was vice minister of the Revenue Board and minister of the Imperial Household.

sentences.zh: 李宗昉，字芝齡，江蘇山陽人。

translations.literal: Li Zongfang, style name Zhiling, was a native of Shanyang in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zongfang, courtesy name Zhiling, came from Shanyang in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶七年一甲二名進士，授編修，典陝甘鄉試。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Jiaqing he placed second in the first class of jinshi, was appointed compiler, and presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took second place in the first class of jinshi in Jiaqing's seventh year, became a compiler, and chief examiner for Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 大考二等，擢贊善。

translations.literal: In the grand examination he placed second class and was promoted to tutor.
translations.idiomatic: He ranked second class in the palace examination and was made tutor in the Eastern Palace.

sentences.zh: 督貴州學政，累遷侍讀學士，督浙江學政。

translations.literal: He served as superintendent of Guizhou education, was repeatedly promoted to reader in the Hanlin Academy, and served as superintendent of Zhejiang education.
translations.idiomatic: He was Guizhou educational commissioner, rose to Hanlin reader, then Zhejiang educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 歷詹事、內閣學士。

translations.literal: He served as mentor and grand secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He held the posts of mentor and grand secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 道光元年，授禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Daoguang he was appointed vice minister of rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang's first year he became vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 次年，典會試，又典江西鄉試，留學政。

translations.literal: The following year he presided over the metropolitan examination, then the Jiangxi provincial examination, and remained as educational commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he ran the metropolitan and Jiangxi provincial examinations and stayed on as educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 值大水，歲饑，與巡撫籌賑務，多所全活。

translations.literal: Great floods came and the year was famine-stricken; with the governor he planned relief and saved many lives.
translations.idiomatic: When severe floods brought famine he worked with the governor on relief and saved many lives.

sentences.zh: 調戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was moved to vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 初，宗昉督學貴州時，巡撫議丈全省田為增賦計，民情惶駭，會檄學官徵集圖書，得御史包承祚奏疏，乾隆初，學政鄒一桂請丈田，而承祚奏駁之，極言黔中山多平地少，民每虛佔不毛之地，胥吏高下其手，以丈高下不可準之田，賦未必增，民受其害。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Zongfang was superintendent of Guizhou education, the governor proposed surveying all fields in the province to increase taxes; the people were terrified; just then an order went to educational officials to collect documents, and he obtained a memorial by Censor Bao Chengzuo: in early Qianlong, Educational Commissioner Zou Yigui had requested field surveys, but Chengzuo memorialized in rebuttal, stating at length that in Qian there are many mountains and little flat land, that people often falsely claim barren ground, that clerks manipulated figures, that surveying fields of uneven height could not be accurate, that revenue might not increase, and that the people would suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, as Guizhou educational commissioner, he had faced a governor's plan to survey the whole province for higher taxes, which terrified the populace; collecting documents on order, he found Censor Bao Chengzuo's memorial from early Qianlong rebutting Commissioner Zou Yigui's survey proposal—arguing that Guizhou's mountains left little arable land, that people falsely claimed wasteland, that clerks manipulated figures, that uneven terrain could not be measured fairly, that revenue might not rise, and that the people would suffer.

sentences.zh: 部議停止，宗昉持以示巡撫曰：「此事學臣嘗奏之，被駁。

translations.literal: The ministry deliberated to stop it; Zongfang took it to show the governor, saying: "This matter the educational commissioner once memorialized and was rejected.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry had halted the plan; Zongfang showed the governor the document, saying, "An educational commissioner once proposed this and was rejected.

sentences.zh: 今必解其所駁乃可。

translations.literal: Now you must explain what was rejected before it can proceed."
translations.idiomatic: You must answer that rejection before reviving it."

sentences.zh: 」巡撫亦悟，事得寢。

translations.literal: The governor also understood, and the matter was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: The governor took the point and the scheme was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 至是，官戶部，署巡撫麟慶因復奏上其事，部援故事詳覆之，乃定議不行。

translations.literal: At this time, holding office in the Ministry of Revenue, Acting Governor Lin Qing again memorialized the matter; the ministry cited precedent in detailed reply, and it was finally decided not to proceed.
translations.idiomatic: Now in the Revenue ministry, Acting Governor Lin Qing revived the proposal; the ministry cited precedent in a full reply and finally blocked it.

sentences.zh: 歷工部、吏部侍郎，兼管國子監、順天府尹事。

translations.literal: He served as vice minister of works and personnel, and concurrently managed the Directorate of Education and the Shuntian prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was vice minister of works and personnel, concurrently overseeing the Directorate of Education and Shuntian prefecture.

sentences.zh: 自七年至十年，典順天鄉試二，會試一，浙江鄉試一，得士稱盛。

translations.literal: From the seventh to the tenth year he twice presided over the Shuntian provincial examination, once over the metropolitan examination, and once over the Zhejiang provincial examination; the scholars selected were praised as outstanding.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh through tenth years he twice ran Shuntian's provincial exam, once the metropolitan exam, and once Zhejiang's—each cohort acclaimed.

sentences.zh: 擢左都御史、禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was promoted Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He became Left Censor-in-Chief and Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，以疾乞休。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he begged to retire on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he retired for illness.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒，依例賜卹。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died; condolence payments were granted according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the twenty-sixth year and received standard mourning grants.

sentences.zh: 姚元之，字伯昂，安徽桐城人。

translations.literal: Yao Yuanzhi, style name Bo'ang, was a native of Tongcheng in Anhui.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Yuanzhi, courtesy name Bo'ang, came from Tongcheng in Anhui.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十年進士，選庶吉士，授編修，典陝甘鄉試。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Jiaqing he passed the jinshi examination, was selected as a Hanlin bachelor, was appointed compiler, and presided over the Shaanxi-Gansu provincial examination.
translations.idiomatic: He took his jinshi in Jiaqing's tenth year, entered the Hanlin Academy, became a compiler, and examined Shaanxi-Gansu.

sentences.zh: 入直南書房。

translations.literal: He entered service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: He served in the Southern Study.

sentences.zh: 給事中花傑劾戴衢亨、英和援引，詔元之文字本佳，斥傑詆訐，尋亦罷元之入直。

translations.literal: Censor Hua Jie impeached Dai Quheng and Yinghe for patronage; an edict said Yuanzhi's writing was originally excellent, rebuked Jie for slander, but soon also removed Yuanzhi from service in the Southern Study.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Hua Jie accused Dai Quheng and Yinghe of patronage; the throne praised Yuanzhi's prose and rebuked Jie for slander, yet soon removed Yuanzhi from the Southern Study as well.

sentences.zh: 十七年，大考一等，擢侍講。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, in the grand examination he placed first class and was promoted expositor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he ranked first class in the palace examination and became expositor.

sentences.zh: 復以武英殿刊刻聖訓有誤，仍降編修。

translations.literal: Again, because the Wuying Hall printing of the Sacred Instructions had errors, he was still demoted to compiler.
translations.idiomatic: Errors in the Wuying Hall printing of the Sacred Instructions nonetheless cost him his rank and he was demoted to compiler.

sentences.zh: 十九年，督河南學政，疏禁坊刻類典等書以杜剿襲；

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he served as superintendent of Henan education and memorialized to ban workshop-printed compendia and similar books to stop plagiarism;
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year, as Henan educational commissioner, he banned commercial compendia and similar books to curb plagiarism;

sentences.zh: 又密陳河南與安徽、湖北交界地多捻匪，陳州、汝寧鹽運迥殊，土匪把持：並嘉納之。

translations.literal: he also secretly reported that on Henan's borders with Anhui and Hubei there were many Nian bandits, that Chen and Ru salt transport differed greatly, and that local ruffians controlled trade: all were commended and accepted.
translations.idiomatic: he also secretly reported heavy Nian bandit activity on Henan's borders with Anhui and Hubei, and ruffian control of Chen-Ru salt routes—the court welcomed both reports.

sentences.zh: 累遷內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to grand secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to grand secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 道光十三年，授工部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Daoguang he was appointed vice minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: In Daoguang's thirteenth year he became vice minister of works.

sentences.zh: 疏陳台灣營務積弊，窩娼聚賭，械鬥殺人，操演僱人替代，詔下閩督嚴察整頓。

translations.literal: He memorialized on accumulated abuses in Taiwan garrison affairs—brothels, gambling dens, armed brawls and killings, and hiring substitutes for drill—and an edict ordered the Fujian governor to investigate and rectify strictly.
translations.idiomatic: He exposed Taiwan garrison abuses—brothels, gambling, armed killings, and hired stand-ins at drill—and the Fujian governor was ordered to crack down.

sentences.zh: 調戶部，又調刑部。

translations.literal: He was transferred to revenue, then again to punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He moved to Revenue, then to Punishments.

sentences.zh: 迭典順天、江西鄉試。

translations.literal: He repeatedly presided over the Shuntian and Jiangxi provincial examinations.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly served as chief examiner for Shuntian and Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 督浙江學政，未滿，十八年，擢左都御史，召回京。

translations.literal: He served as superintendent of Zhejiang education; before his term ended, in the eighteenth year he was promoted Left Censor-in-Chief and recalled to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: As Zhejiang educational commissioner, before his term ended he was made Left Censor-in-Chief in the eighteenth year and recalled.

sentences.zh: 尋以南昌知府張寅為江西巡撫裕泰劾罷，元之為寅疏辯，臚陳政績，請查辦，詔斥冒昧，降二級調用。

translations.literal: Soon after, because Nanchang Prefect Zhang Yin had been impeached and dismissed by Jiangxi Governor Yutai, Yuanzhi memorialized in Zhang's defense, listing his achievements and requesting investigation; an edict rebuked his presumption and demoted him two ranks for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangxi Governor Yutai impeached Nanchang Prefect Zhang Yin, Yuanzhi defended Zhang, citing his record and asking for review; the throne called him presumptuous and demoted him two ranks.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，海防方亟，疏陳廣東形勢，豫籌戰守，下靖逆將軍奕山等採行。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, when coastal defense was urgent, he memorialized on Guangdong's strategic situation and planned defense in advance; it was sent down to Pacification General Yishan and others for adoption.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, with coastal defense urgent, he outlined Guangdong's strategic position and proposed defensive measures, which Yishan and others were ordered to implement.

sentences.zh: 授內閣學士。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，京察，以年衰休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, at the capital evaluation, he retired on grounds of advanced age.
translations.idiomatic: At the twenty-third year's capital evaluation he retired for old age.

sentences.zh: 元之學於族祖鼐，文章爾雅，書畫並工。

translations.literal: Yuanzhi studied under his clansman Nai; his essays were refined, and he was skilled in both calligraphy and painting.
translations.idiomatic: Trained by his kinsman Yao Nai, he wrote refined prose and excelled at calligraphy and painting.

sentences.zh: 習於掌故，館閣推為祭酒。

translations.literal: Well versed in institutional precedent, he was regarded in the academies as their doyen.
translations.idiomatic: Fluent in institutional precedent, the academies hailed him as their doyen.

sentences.zh: 愛士好事，穆彰阿素重之。

translations.literal: He loved scholars and delighted in good causes; Mujangga had always valued him.
translations.idiomatic: He championed scholars and good works; Mujangga had long esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 後以論洋務不合，乃被黜。

translations.literal: Later, because his views on foreign affairs did not accord, he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Later his views on foreign affairs fell out of favor and he was pushed out.

sentences.zh: 咸豐二年，卒。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianfeng he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Xianfeng.

sentences.zh: 何汝霖，字雨人，江蘇江寧人。

translations.literal: He Rulin, style name Yuren, was a native of Jiangning in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: He Rulin, courtesy name Yuren, came from Jiangning in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 拔貢，考授工部七品小京官。

translations.literal: Selected as a tribute student, he passed examination and was appointed a seventh-rank secretary in the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: A tribute graduate, he passed selection and became a seventh-rank secretary in Works.

sentences.zh: 中式道光五年舉人，充軍機章京，累遷郎中。

translations.literal: He passed the provincial examination in the fifth year of Daoguang, served as a Grand Council clerk, and was repeatedly promoted to director.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the provincial exam in Daoguang's fifth year, joined the Grand Council staff, and rose to director.

sentences.zh: 歷內閣侍讀學士、大理寺少卿。

translations.literal: He served as reader in the Grand Secretariat and vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was a Grand Secretariat reader and vice president of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 偕侍郎恩桂按事浙江，查勘南河料垛。

translations.literal: Together with Vice Minister En Gui he investigated affairs in Zhejiang and inspected stockpiles on the Southern Canal.
translations.idiomatic: With Vice Minister En Gui he investigated Zhejiang affairs and inspected Southern Canal stockpiles.

sentences.zh: 命在軍機大臣上行走，歷宗人府丞、副都御史。

translations.literal: He was ordered to serve on the Grand Council under the grand ministers, and served as vice director of the Imperial Clan Court and vice censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned to the Grand Council under the grand ministers and served as Imperial Clan vice director and vice censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，授兵部侍郎，調戶部。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was appointed vice minister of war and transferred to revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he became vice minister of war, then moved to revenue.

sentences.zh: 偕大學士敬徵勘東河工程。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Secretary Jingzheng he surveyed the Eastern Canal works.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Grand Secretary Jingzheng in surveying Eastern Canal works.

sentences.zh: 二十五年，擢兵部尚書。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fifth year he was promoted Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fifth year he became Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 值太后七旬萬壽，汝霖母丁年九十，五世同堂，賜御書扁額，尋以母憂歸。

translations.literal: When the empress dowager's seventieth birthday was celebrated, Rulin's mother Lady Ding was ninety, with five generations under one roof; an imperial inscription on a plaque was bestowed; soon after he returned home for mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: At the empress dowager's seventieth birthday, Rulin's mother Lady Ding was ninety with five generations in one household; the emperor bestowed an inscribed plaque; he soon left office to mourn her.

sentences.zh: 江蘇大水，命在籍襄治賑務。

translations.literal: Jiangsu suffered great floods; he was ordered while at home to assist in relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiangsu flooded he was ordered home to help with relief.

sentences.zh: 先是，總督陶澍於江寧立豐備倉以備荒，縣令虧挪穀價，大吏許以他款抵。

translations.literal: Earlier, Governor Tao Shu had established at Jiangning the Fengbei granary against famine; magistrates had embezzled grain funds, and high officials allowed other funds to offset the loss.
translations.idiomatic: Governor Tao Shu had built Jiangning's Fengbei granary for famine years, but magistrates had embezzled grain funds and superiors let other accounts cover the shortfall.

sentences.zh: 汝霖曰：「倉穀以備兇。

translations.literal: Rulin said: "Granary grain is to guard against famine.
translations.idiomatic: Rulin said, "Granary grain exists for famine.

sentences.zh: 今荒像如此，汝霖不敢欺朝廷，當各為奏上。

translations.literal: With famine now like this, Rulin dare not deceive the court; each case should be memorialized separately."
translations.idiomatic: With distress this severe I cannot deceive the throne; each shortfall must be reported separately."

sentences.zh: 」乃以給賑用。

translations.literal: " The grain was then used for relief.
translations.idiomatic: " The grain was released for relief.

sentences.zh: 服闋，命以一品頂戴署禮部侍郎，尋署戶部尚書，仍直軍機處，授禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was ordered to serve with first-rank insignia as acting vice minister of rites, soon after acting Minister of Revenue, still serving on the Grand Council, then appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he returned with first-rank insignia as acting vice minister of rites, soon acting Minister of Revenue, still on the Grand Council, then Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 汝霖久襄樞務，資勞己深，尚書陳孚恩由章京躋大臣，駸用事，厭汝霖居其前。

translations.literal: Rulin had long assisted in council affairs and his seniority was deep; Minister Chen Fu'en had risen from a council clerk to grand minister and gradually dominated affairs, resenting Rulin's precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Long experienced in council work, Rulin outranked Minister Chen Fu'en, who had climbed from council clerk to power and resented standing below him.

sentences.zh: 汝霖年逾七十，一日在直，觸火爐幾僕。

translations.literal: Rulin was over seventy; one day on duty he bumped a brazier and nearly fell.
translations.idiomatic: Past seventy, he once stumbled against a brazier while on council duty.

sentences.zh: 孚恩笑曰：「人當避爐，爐豈能避人？

translations.literal: Fu'en laughed and said: "People should avoid the brazier; can a brazier avoid people?"
translations.idiomatic: Fu'en laughed, "People should dodge the stove—can the stove dodge people?"

sentences.zh: 」汝霖知其諷己，咸豐二年，以足疾乞罷直，許之。

translations.literal: " Rulin knew he was being mocked; in the second year of Xianfeng he begged to leave council duty on grounds of foot ailment; permission was granted.
translations.idiomatic: " Rulin took the jibe; in Xianfeng's second year he asked to leave council duty for foot trouble and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒，諡恪慎，祀鄉賢。

translations.literal: Soon after he died; posthumous title Kejin; enshrined among local worthies.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died, received the posthumous name Kejin, and entered the local worthies' shrine.

sentences.zh: 子兆瀛，浙江鹽運使。

translations.literal: His son Zhaoying was Zhejiang salt transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhaoying was Zhejiang salt transport commissioner.

sentences.zh: 季芝昌，字仙九，江蘇江陰人。

translations.literal: Ji Zhichang, style name Xianjiu, was a native of Jiangyin in Jiangsu.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhichang, courtesy name Xianjiu, came from Jiangyin in Jiangsu.

sentences.zh: 父麟，直隸鉅鹿知縣，居官慈惠。

translations.literal: His father Lin was magistrate of Julu in Zhili and was benevolent in office.
translations.idiomatic: His father Lin, magistrate of Julu in Zhili, governed with kindness.

sentences.zh: 嘉慶十八年，捕邪教，焚其籍，免株連數千人。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year of Jiaqing he arrested heterodox sect members, burned their registers, and spared thousands from implication.
translations.idiomatic: In Jiaqing's eighteenth year he suppressed a heterodox sect, burned its registers, and spared thousands from collective punishment.

sentences.zh: 坐捕匪不力，戍伊犁。

translations.literal: He was penalized for ineffective pursuit of bandits and was banished to Yili.
translations.idiomatic: Punished for failing to catch bandits, he was exiled to Yili.

sentences.zh: 芝昌年逾四十，成道光十二年一甲三名進士，授編修，散館第一。

translations.literal: Zhichang was over forty when he placed third in the first class of jinshi in the twelfth year of Daoguang, was appointed compiler, and ranked first upon leaving the Hanlin Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Past forty, Zhichang took third place in the first class in Daoguang's twelfth year, became a compiler, and topped the Hanlin dispersal examination.

sentences.zh: 未幾，大考第三，擢侍讀，督山東學政。

translations.literal: Soon after, in the grand examination he placed third and was promoted reader, and served as superintendent of Shandong education.
translations.idiomatic: Soon ranked third in the palace examination, he became reader and Shandong educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 十九年，大考复第三，擢少詹事，晉詹事，典江西鄉試，督浙江學政。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year, again third in the grand examination, he was promoted junior mentor, advanced to mentor, presided over the Jiangxi provincial examination, and served as superintendent of Zhejiang education.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he again placed third in the palace exam, rose to junior mentor then mentor, examined Jiangxi, and became Zhejiang educational commissioner.

sentences.zh: 母憂歸，服闋，擢內閣學士。

translations.literal: He returned home for mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was promoted grand secretariat bachelor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning his mother he returned as grand secretariat bachelor.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，授禮部侍郎，督安徽學政，調吏部，又調倉場。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he was appointed vice minister of rites, superintendent of Anhui education, transferred to personnel, then to the grain transport post.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he became vice minister of rites and Anhui educational commissioner, then moved to Personnel and the grain transport post.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，命偕定郡王載銓籌辦長蘆鹽務，清查天津倉庫，疏陳：「蘆鹽積累，各商憚於承運，懸岸至四十餘處。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was ordered with Prince Ding Zaiquan to plan the Changlu salt administration and audit Tianjin granaries; he memorialized: "Changlu salt had accumulated; merchants feared to undertake transport, and salt lay unsold at more than forty sites.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he and Prince Ding Zaiquan reorganized Changlu salt and audited Tianjin granaries, reporting: "Changlu salt had piled up; merchants feared to move it, and stock sat at more than forty depots.

sentences.zh: 請將河南二十四州縣仿淮南例改票鹽，先課後引。

translations.literal: He requested that the twenty-four prefectures and counties of Henan follow the Huainan precedent and switch to ticket salt, collecting tax before issuing transport permits.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that Henan's twenty-four prefectures and counties adopt Huainan's ticket-salt system, taxing before issuing transport permits.

sentences.zh: 直隸二十四州縣限半年招商招販，無商販即責成州縣領運，或由鹽政遴員官運。

translations.literal: For the twenty-four prefectures and counties of Zhili, within half a year merchants should be recruited; if none came, prefectures and counties must undertake transport, or the salt commissioner select officials for government transport.
translations.idiomatic: Zhili's twenty-four jurisdictions were given six months to attract merchants; failing that, prefectures must move salt themselves or the commissioner appoint official carriers.

sentences.zh: 支銷浮費及官役陋規，永遠裁汰。

translations.literal: Extravagant expenses and clerks' customary fees were to be permanently cut.
translations.idiomatic: Extravagant charges and clerks' customary fees were to be abolished permanently.

sentences.zh: 每年應完帑利，灘及通綱額引，與正課一律徵收。

translations.literal: Each year the treasury profit, beach levies, and general quota permits were to be collected together with the main tax.
translations.idiomatic: Annual treasury profits, beach levies, and general quota permits were to be collected with the main salt tax.

sentences.zh: 其協濟補欠充公等項加價名目，概行革除。

translations.literal: Surcharge items such as mutual aid, deficit makeup, and public funds were entirely abolished.
translations.idiomatic: Surcharges for mutual aid, deficit makeup, and public funds were abolished outright.

sentences.zh: 並於各引鹽加斤免課，每斤准其減價敵私。

translations.literal: On each transport permit extra weight was to be tax-free, with each catty allowed a price reduction to compete with smuggled salt.
translations.idiomatic: Each transport permit would carry extra weight tax-free, with a per-catty price cut to undercut smugglers.

sentences.zh: 」詔依議行。

translations.literal: " An edict approved implementation according to the proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " The throne approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，偕大學士耆英赴浙江閱兵，並清查倉庫，籌辦鹽務。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, together with Grand Secretary Qiying he went to Zhejiang to review troops, audit granaries, and plan salt affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he joined Grand Secretary Qiying in Zhejiang to review troops, audit granaries, and reform salt.

sentences.zh: 途經東河、南河，查詢節浮費、裁冗員事宜，奏減東河正款二十萬兩，裁泉河通判、歸河通判，南河每年用款以三百萬兩為率，減省五六十萬兩，並揚運通判於江防廳，改為江運同知，裁丹陽縣丞、靈壁主簿、呂梁洪巡檢，從之。

translations.literal: Passing the Eastern and Southern canals, he inquired into cutting waste and reducing redundant posts; he memorialized to reduce the Eastern Canal regular appropriation by two hundred thousand taels, abolish the Quanhe and Guihe assistant prefects, set the Southern Canal annual budget at three million taels with savings of five or six hundred thousand, transfer the Yangyun assistant prefect to the River Defense Office as Jiangyun sub-prefect, and abolish the Danyang county assistant, Lingbi registrar, and Lüliang Hong inspector; approval was granted.
translations.idiomatic: En route on the Eastern and Southern canals he studied waste and redundant posts, cutting the Eastern Canal budget by two hundred thousand taels, abolishing two assistant prefects, capping the Southern Canal at three million taels with five or six hundred thousand saved, moving one assistant prefect to river defense as sub-prefect, and abolishing three minor posts—all approved.

sentences.zh: 耆英病留清江浦，芝昌獨赴浙江，疏陳變通鹽務章程七事：杭、嘉、紹三所引鹽，分別加斤，止令完交正課；

translations.literal: Qiying fell ill and remained at Qingjiangpu; Zhichang went alone to Zhejiang and memorialized seven items for flexible salt regulations: for salt from the Hang, Jia, and Shao depots, extra weight was to be added separately and only the main tax collected;
translations.idiomatic: Qiying fell ill at Qingjiangpu; Zhichang went on alone to Zhejiang and proposed seven salt reforms: for Hang, Jia, and Shao salt, add weight separately and collect only the main tax;

sentences.zh: 松所引鹽，酌裁科則；

translations.literal: for Song depot salt, rates were to be adjusted;
translations.idiomatic: for Song depot salt, adjust the tax schedule;

sentences.zh: 虛懸口岸，選商接辦，並籌款收鹽；

translations.literal: for vacant transit ports, select merchants to take over and raise funds to purchase salt;
translations.idiomatic: for idle transit ports, assign merchants, raise funds, and buy up stock;

sentences.zh: 緝私責成官商，由運司審覈；

translations.literal: Responsibility for suppressing smuggling was fixed on officials and merchants, to be reviewed by the transport commissioner;
translations.idiomatic: Anti-smuggling duty was assigned to officials and merchants under the transport commissioner's review;

sentences.zh: 緝獲私鹽，分別充賞，及補課作正配銷；

translations.literal: when smuggled salt was seized, rewards were allotted separately, and recovered tax could count toward regular quota sales;
translations.idiomatic: seized contraband salt would be rewarded by grade, and recovered tax could count toward regular quota sales;

sentences.zh: 禁革引地陋規；

translations.literal: customary fees in transit districts were forbidden;
translations.idiomatic: customary fees along transit routes were abolished;

sentences.zh: 覈裁巡驗浮費。

translations.literal: extravagant costs for patrol and inspection were audited and cut.
translations.idiomatic: patrol and inspection surcharges were audited and reduced.

sentences.zh: 尋查州縣倉庫，統計實虧之數，多至三百九十餘萬，請將虧數最多之員，革職，勒追；

translations.literal: Soon after he inspected prefectural and county granaries and tallied actual deficits, which in many cases reached more than 3.9 million; he requested that officials with the largest deficits be dismissed and compelled to make restitution;
translations.idiomatic: He soon audited prefectural and county granaries, finding deficits as high as 3.9 million taels, and asked that the worst offenders be dismissed and forced to repay;

sentences.zh: 不足，則由原任上司按成分賠，或由本省各官分成提補；

translations.literal: if insufficient, then former superiors should compensate by graded shares, or officials of the province should contribute in shares to make up the loss;
translations.idiomatic: shortfalls were to be recovered from former superiors by graded shares or from provincial officials in joint contribution;

sentences.zh: 其有欠在胥吏者，尤嚴補追，毋任倖免：並從之。

translations.literal: where debts lay with clerks, pursuit was especially strict, with no allowance for escape: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: clerk debts were to be pursued especially hard with no leniency—all approved.

sentences.zh: 授山西巡撫，未一月，召署吏部侍郎，命在軍機大臣上行走。

translations.literal: He was appointed governor of Shanxi; within a month he was summoned to act as vice minister of personnel and ordered to serve on the Grand Council under the grand ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Made Shanxi governor, within a month he was recalled as acting vice minister of personnel and assigned to the Grand Council.

sentences.zh: 尋授戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon after he was appointed vice minister of revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He soon became vice minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 三十年，擢左都御史。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was promoted Left Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he was made Left Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 咸豐元年，出為閩浙總督。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianfeng he went out as governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianfeng's first year he became governor-general of Fujian and Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 艇匪在浙洋劫掠山東兵船，被剿遁閩洋，遣水師截擊，賊眾畏罪投誠，分別安置。

translations.literal: Boat bandits in Zhejiang waters plundered a Shandong military vessel; pursued and driven into Fujian waters, he dispatched naval forces to intercept; the bandits, fearing punishment, surrendered and were settled separately.
translations.idiomatic: Boat pirates in Zhejiang waters raided a Shandong military ship; driven into Fujian waters, he sent the navy to intercept; the gang, fearing punishment, surrendered and was resettled in groups.

sentences.zh: 二年，兼署福州將軍。

translations.literal: In the second year he concurrently acted as commander at Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he also acted as Fuzhou commander.

sentences.zh: 疏請停罷捐納舉人、附生之例；

translations.literal: He memorialized to stop the practice of purchasing juren and supplemental licentiate degrees through contributions;
translations.idiomatic: He asked to end the sale of juren and supplemental licentiate degrees by contribution;

sentences.zh: 又奏禁鹽商代銷官運，以杜取巧：並從之。

translations.literal: he also memorialized to forbid salt merchants from substituting for government transport to stop opportunism: all were approved.
translations.idiomatic: and to forbid salt merchants from substituting for government transport to block loopholes—both approved.

sentences.zh: 尋以疾乞休。

translations.literal: Soon after he begged to retire on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired for illness.

sentences.zh: 芝昌以文字受宣宗特達之知，嘗曰：「汝為文，行所無事，譬之於射，五矢無一失。

translations.literal: Zhichang, because of his writing, won the Xuanzong Emperor's special favor; the emperor once said: "When you write, you do what is natural, like archery—of five arrows not one misses."
translations.idiomatic: Zhichang's prose won Emperor Xuanzong's special regard; the emperor once told him, "Your writing does only what is needed, like archery—five arrows, five hits."

sentences.zh: 」及查辦長蘆、兩浙鹽務稱旨，遂驟進膺樞務。

translations.literal: When his investigation of Changlu and the two Zhe salt administrations pleased the throne, he was suddenly advanced to council affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His handling of Changlu and the two Zhe salt systems pleased the throne, and he was suddenly thrust into Grand Council work.

sentences.zh: 甫數月，宣宗崩，文宗猶欲用之，畀以外任。

translations.literal: After only a few months the Xuanzong Emperor died; the Wenzong Emperor still wished to use him and gave him an outside appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Within months Xuanzong died; Wenzong still meant to use him and sent him to a provincial post.

sentences.zh: 未一歲，謝職歸。

translations.literal: In less than a year he resigned and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he resigned and went home.

sentences.zh: 久之，卒於家，未予卹典。

translations.literal: After a long time he died at home; no condolence grant was given.
translations.idiomatic: He died at home years later without receiving standard mourning honors.

sentences.zh: 光緒初，署閩浙總督文煜奏陳政績，追諡文敏。

translations.literal: In early Guangxu, Acting Governor-General Wen Yu of Fujian and Zhejiang memorialized his achievements; he was posthumously given the title Wenmin.
translations.idiomatic: In early Guangxu, Acting Governor-General Wen Yu cited his record and he received the posthumous name Wenmin.

sentences.zh: 子念詒，道光三十年進士，官編修。

translations.literal: His son Nianyi, jinshi in the thirtieth year of Daoguang, served as compiler.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nianyi, a Daoguang thirtieth-year jinshi, was a Hanlin compiler.

sentences.zh: 孫邦楨，同治十二年進士，官至福建布政使。

translations.literal: His grandson Bangzhen, jinshi in the twelfth year of Tongzhi, rose to Fujian financial commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Grandson Bangzhen, a Tongzhi twelfth-year jinshi, became Fujian financial commissioner.

sentences.zh: 論曰：承平，士大夫平進而致列卿，或以恪謹稱，或以文學顯，固不能盡有所建樹；

translations.literal: The commentary says: In times of peace, scholar-officials advanced by routine to ministerial rank, some praised for scrupulous care, some distinguished for literary talent—they could not all achieve great deeds;
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In peaceful times officials rose by routine to high office, some noted for diligence, some for letters—not all could leave a major mark;

sentences.zh: 或餘澤延世，子孫復繼簪纓，若白鎔、那清安、升寅諸人是也。

translations.literal: yet some left lingering blessings through generations, with sons and grandsons again inheriting official rank, as with Bai Rong, Na Qing'an, Sheng Yin, and the like.
translations.idiomatic: yet some families' favor lasted generations, sons and grandsons again wearing court insignia, as with Bai Rong, Na Qing'an, and Sheng Yin.

sentences.zh: 季芝昌晚遭殊遇，已值宣宗倦勤之年，暫任兼圻，奉身而退，其見幾知止者耶？

translations.literal: Ji Zhichang late in life met extraordinary favor, but it was already the year when the Xuanzong Emperor grew weary of rule; he briefly held concurrent frontier command, then withdrew while preserving himself—was this not seeing the moment and knowing when to stop?
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhichang's late favor came as Xuanzong wearied of rule; he briefly held a frontier post, then withdrew intact—did he not read the moment and know when to stop?
